title: Right-angle-free sets in the tetrahedral grid
statement: Let the tetrahedral grid F_N be the points a e1 + b e2 + c e3 with integers a, b, c >= 0 and a + b + c <= N - 1, where e1, e2, e3 are unit vectors at 60 degrees to each other: N(N+1)(N+2)/6 points of the face-centred cubic lattice forming a tetrahedron of side N - 1; the squared distance is da^2 + db^2 + dc^2 + da db + db dc + dc da. Determine the largest number of points of the tetrahedral grid F_N such that no three of them form a right angle (no three points p, q, r with (q - p).(r - p) = 0), as a function of N. The exact values are known (ours) for N <= 6; the headline cell is N = 8: find 17 or more such points of the region of side 8.
submission: Text file: one point 'a b c' per line, a point of the region of side 8 (lines starting with # are ignored).
score: the number of points (larger is better)

best_known.source: Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 10 November 2026: 16 points of the region of side 8 with no right angle (no three points p, q, r with (q - p).(r - p) = 0), the best set CP-SAT found in 10 seconds, started from the set for side N - 1 (tools/lattice_sets.py)

context: A set of points is right-angle-free when no three of its points form a right angle. Gamble, Pulleyblank, Reed and Shepherd (1995) studied the largest right-angle-free subsets of the plane and of the square lattice, and related work (Junger and Pulleyblank) shows the problem NP-hard for general point sets; sets without isosceles right triangles in the n x n grid are a separate, active question (OEIS A271906; arXiv:2607.22828, 2026). In the face-centred cubic lattice right angles occur in many directions (the three cube axes of the crystal, for example, are lattice directions perpendicular to each other); how fast the largest right-angle-free sets of the tetrahedral grid grow is open.
references: B. Gamble, W. Pulleyblank, B. Reed, B. Shepherd, Right angle free subsets in the plane, Graphs and Combinatorics 11 (1995) 121-129
A Salem-Spencer-type construction for large subsets of integer grids with no isosceles right triangles, arXiv:2607.22828 (2026)
OEIS A271906 (largest subsets of the n x n grid with no right isosceles triangle)

novelty.verdict: new question for this lattice: right-angle-free subsets are studied for the square lattice (Gamble, Pulleyblank, Reed and Shepherd 1995; Junger and Pulleyblank) and isosceles right triangles in the square grid (A271906); no result was found for the tetrahedral grid, and its first values are not in the OEIS as such (the sequences matching them, A014687, A125204, A305594, A172022, are unrelated and agree on these few terms by coincidence).
closest: B. Gamble, W. Pulleyblank, B. Reed and B. Shepherd (1995): right-angle-free subsets of the plane and of the square lattice; another lattice.
OEIS A271906 and arXiv:2607.22828: no isosceles right triangle in the square grid, a weaker condition in another lattice.

baseline.text: 16 for N = 8, held by Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 10 November 2026: the points in `refs/tetra-right.txt` (the best set CP-SAT found in 10 seconds, started from the set for side N - 1 (tools/lattice_sets.py)). Exact values for N = 2..6: 4, 4, 8, 10, 14 (CP-SAT (OR-Tools 9.15, one worker) proved the optimum of the 0/1 model in tools/lattice_sets.py).
